horizon.notes: 44 min cold (22:48-23:32), absence loaded once at 23:33, 22 min on return. Watched run 1 (~8 min at 1x) and run 2 (~4 min at 1x) at slow, the rest at fast/auto/skip. Deaths read: goblin warlord D5, pink jelly D7, gas D8. Own edits: foes>=3 -> retreat/to corridor (with reorder), depth>=5 -> return (tried bank), foe: boss -> return then attack boss, foe: telegraph -> retreat (tried attack telegraph, to corridor, kite), foes>=1 -> shoot nearest (reverted). Also switched class to ranger, bought card: kite archers, tapped one offered patch (hp<20% -> return).

killCriteria.$notes: No crash; state survived the absence reload. The 20m rest never blocked a send while I was present and nothing is sold to skip it. Default rules forecast D6 0%; my 'foe: boss -> attack boss' moved D6 to 64% and the overnight lineage slew the warlord and reached D7, so editing is not pointless. All three deaths I read were addressable by the vocabulary (a heal, a return-at-20%, a corridor). The return screen had 14 deaths, 8 new foes, a boss kill and 16 marks of unlocks to decide on.

criterion.delayedRecall: same-day: I sent a fresh ranger with my 'run from anything that winds up, fight in doorways, bail at 20%' set and watched him dodge two ogre wind-ups on D4 with 'R3 · retreat'. On D5 he walked into the Goblin Warlord and my boss rule made him swing: 11, 7, 3 HP. At 3 HP the return-at-20% rule I had taken off the last death fired and he walked out with $63; the reel wrote 'The Goblin Warlord waits. Down to 3 HP.'

probes.clarity: I always knew the goal (get deeper, bring gold home, earn marks) and the forecast bars moved the instant I dragged a rule, but 'bank' vs 'return' had no explanation, the send button went silent-grey at '7/6' rows, and the run showed $94 while the reel said 'Returned with $56' and camp said $69.
probes.decisions: Ordering 'foes >= 3 -> to corridor' above 'foes >= 1 -> attack nearest' took D3/D4 from 98% to 100%; choosing 'foe: telegraph -> retreat' over 'attack telegraph' moved the ogre share from 41% to 17% but pushed archers to 43%; I would make both again.
probes.mastery: An hour in I knew that a rule below 'foes >= 1' never fires, that 'ogre winds up' is the cue my retreat rule answers, and that 'attack heavy / attack gas / attack splitter' appear in the verb sheet only after the ledger marks those foes studied.
probes.tension: Hero 17 went 11 -> 7 -> 3 HP against the Warlord with '$63 · return at 20%' in the header before 'R1 · return' fired, and the overnight push at a forecast '64%' came back as '14 DEATHS, 0 RETURNED'.
probes.feel: Hits are a red caption ('-3 gas', '-2 jackal') and a hero sprite that is bigger than the tiles; at 1x the header changed roughly six times a minute with 20-30 s stretches of 'pick up'; audio: unassessed (none).
probes.surprise: The vault ('A vault: three under a cage. The vault opens: choose one.'), the ogre wind-up, jellies splitting to three, gas at 2 HP and a monkey that 'stole the darkness scroll' each showed up once; D1-D4 in every watched run was the same rat-jackal-goblin walk.
probes.expression: My set is 'retreat from anything that telegraphs, fight in doorways at three foes, swing at the boss, bail at 20%'; the '[card] kite archers' row in the middle of it is a black box I paid 3 marks for and cannot open.
probes.story: The reel wrote 'The Goblin Warlord waits. / Down to 3 HP. / Returned with $37.' and the overnight lines read 'Pink jellies cornered him to 1 HP; R3 backed; died to jelly.'
probes.pacing: In-run at 1x a D5 trip took 8-12 minutes with 20-30 s of nothing but 'pick up'; a check-in was read-the-report, one or two edits, buy a $40 heal, send, about 5-8 minutes and ending on a chosen send; the '▶▶|' button stepped rather than skipped, and the 'VAULT 0/0' sheet appears with nothing to choose on every return.
probes.failure: 'goblin warlord · D5 · 1 over · 4 unknown unused · gap' with five rows of 'R2 attack nearest hp 1 foes 4' told me exactly what happened and what did not fire; the next hero was ready instantly; the 'morgue' button did nothing on any death screen.
probes.autonomy: Nobody asked me to bank at D5 or to switch the fresh hero to ranger; both were mine, and the header showed 'return at D5' as my goal.
probes.progression: Within a run gold and XP grew ('ranger +31 · L1') but no hero ever left L1; between runs marks bought +1 row, +1 vault, ranger and a card, the ledger filled with 'studied' foes, and learned facts grew the verb sheet; 'auto: restock' cost 4 marks and left no visible trace of what it now does.
probes.aesthetic: A black field with warm-olive brick and a chunky sword-and-shield sprite saying 'LET'S SEE' over a scroll; coherent and dim, not somewhere to sit.
probes.return: I came back to '14 RUNS · D7 BEST · ◆+16 · 14 DEATHS · rested 280m', 'boss: goblin warlord' in BESTS, eight new LEARNED chips and five reel lines, and spent 16 marks on a row, restock and ranger plus wrote the telegraph rule; I would not rather have stayed, but 'open' showed one death and the other thirteen were unreachable.
probes.attribution: My hero died to jellies because my 'to corridor' rule kept backing him into the same spot at 2 HP, and he lived against the Warlord because my return-at-20% rule outranked my boss rule; two of the three deaths I read ended on the shipped 'attack nearest' that I chose to keep at the bottom.

axes.proxy: time-to-first-rule-edit; misread rate on the trace
axes.note: Goal and feedback are there: forecast bars and the killer list update live on every drag, the run header carries my rule ('$60 · return at D5'). Adequate not strong because of routine friction: 'bank' vs 'return' unexplained, '1 over' unexplained, send silently disabled at '7/6', three different gold numbers per run ($94 in-run, 'Returned with $56', $69 at camp), bought unlocks (path: bones, auto: restock) vanish with no trace.

Every check-in had a foreseeable trade-off I would defend: rule order (a shadowed rule changed nothing until dragged above 'foes >= 1'), retreat vs corridor vs attack for telegraph (ogre 17% / 18% / 41%), bank at D5 (78%) vs push to D6 (64%), heal vs bow from the vault, row vs bones vs card for 5 marks. Lapse: the forecast wobbles +/-10 points between reads of near-identical sets (D5 43% vs 58%), so close calls are guesses.

I learned shadowing, the telegraph cue, and that facts grow the verb sheet; but heroes never leave L1 and the D6+ wall stayed (forecast D6 never above 20% after the return), and the card I bought taught me nothing I could read.

Stakes were mine and resolved when I looked: 'death: lose all' vs 'return at D5', the 3 HP Warlord exit, the 64% push carried into the night that came back 14 dead. Lapse: at 1x most of a run is 'pick up' walking with nothing at risk, and the fights that matter resolve in four seconds at fast.

axes.proxy: frame time; events per minute at 1x
axes.note: Readable but flat: kills are a caption, the killing blow gets a red '-3 gas' and nothing else; ~6 header events a minute at 1x with 20-30 s dead stretches. Audio unassessed (none in build).

axes.proxy: death-cause entropy; distinct situations per run
axes.note: Directly seen: the caged vault choice, the ogre wind-up, splitting jellies, gas at 2 HP, a boss 'counter: known'; the ogre and the boss each changed a rule I wrote. Most of the variety arrived as reel lines from offline runs; every watched D1-D4 was the same rat-jackal-goblin walk.

I can describe my set without the game's words (dodge wind-ups, doorway fighting, swing at the boss, bail at 20%) and a shoot/kite ranger was a defensible other way. Kept from strong: 3 of 7 rows are shipped defaults or patches, the class switch changed only the verb list, and one row is an opaque card.

The reel carries a turn: 'The Goblin Warlord waits. / Down to 3 HP. / Returned with $37.'; the overnight lines are three-beat and name the rule ('R3 backed; died to jelly'); the chronicle line for hero 1 reads as an epitaph. Lapse: the chronicle logged only the death, not the two returns; the reel's gold number contradicts the run.

axes.proxy: run length; check-in length; dead time at 1x
axes.note: In-run: 8-12 min to D5 at 1x with 20-30 s dead stretches; fast/auto make it 1-2 min. Check-in: 5-8 min, ends on a chosen send. Cadence: 20 m rest per hero gives 14 runs overnight; a 20-minute absence would be one run at most. Friction: 'VAULT 0/0' sheet with nothing to pick on every return, '▶▶|' steps instead of skipping, 'rest 20m' label with no visible effect.

axes.proxy: share of deaths with a matched-rule trace
axes.note: Cause, margin and the rule that fired on each of the last five turns on one screen ('R2 attack nearest hp 1 foes 4', 'R3 to corridor hp 2 foes 3'), a 'gap' chip, patches with survive %, and the next hero ready at once. Lapse: 'morgue' does nothing on any death screen and 'base 92%' on a death is not explained.
Bank-at-D5, push, class switch and which bones to chase were self-set goals the game did not ask for; there is no map or route choice beyond depth.

Both layers observed: within-run gold/XP/items, between-run marks -> rows, vault, ranger, card, ledger 'studied' chips and new verbs. Cannot exceed adequate: automation-as-reward ('auto: restock') showed no observable effect, XP never produced a level ('+31 · L1'), and marks came only from depth records and deaths (two safe returns paid ◆0).
Coherent dim-olive brick dungeon, chunky sprite, monospace camp; readable at phone size; no sound; not a place I would idle in.

axes.proxy: offline yield vs active; decisions pending on return
axes.note: Return screen up in ~4 s with 14 runs, D7, ◆+16, boss slain, 8 new foes, 12 bone piles and 5 reel lines; PENDING listed affordable unlocks; I spent 16 marks and wrote a rule within five minutes. Lapse: only one of the 14 deaths was openable ('open' -> pink jelly; 'morgue' dead), and pressing send resumed a half-finished offline run at D7 with the class I had just switched.

axes.proxy: share of deaths attributable to a rule the player wrote
axes.note: Retelling is first-person throughout (my return rule, my corridor rule, my boss rule); the reel names rules ('R4 attacked; died to gas'); the trace let me say the jelly death was my 'to corridor' row and the Warlord escape was my priority order. Lapse: two of three read deaths ended on the shipped 'attack nearest' and the card row could have been acting without my knowing.
